title: Review of the digestion-driven predator ecology (SIEXD): replicates on fresh seed 5 at 256^2 (prey 67 persistent splits gen 4, predators 40 gen 3), the predator-free twin stays frozen (0 splits), and predators dissolve within 800 t of prey removal with their material kept
summary: Read world.py: prey material condenses only up its fuel-made catalysis product and is remade from waste; predator material is conserved, miscible on its own and condenses only up its digestion product q, and drifts down the fuel gradient by a written nonreciprocal taxis (chiF 0.5). labkit, 256^2, seed 5, t=12000, default window: prey 187 bodies at the end, 104 persistent tracks, 67 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.40, 320 moving tracks; predators 187, 87 persistent tracks, 40 persistent splits, generation 3, merge/split 0.20. Matched predator-free twin (pred_on 0, same seed, grid, duration): 158 frozen prey, 0 splits, 1 moving track. Prey-removal fork at t=6000 (drive.py, 128^2, seed 5): predators 46 -> 45 -> 31 -> 4 -> 0 at t=6000/6200/6400/6600/6800, mean predator material 0.11 -> 0.10, while the fed run keeps 46-54. Named lineage on my seed: predator 46 -> 333 -> 386 -> 424 (pack256/pred_ancestry.png), generation 3 at t=8100, alive to t=10800; every division I looked at is a joint fission with a prey.

seeds_run.result: pass (256^2 labkit, twin, and 128^2 prey-removal fork)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed (each 256^2 run takes ~28 min). I checked E only for the predators, not the prey's fuel cut. Predator divisions are joint fissions with a prey (the predator is drawn out between the two prey daughters), and the prey divide only with predators attached (twin: 0 splits), so the dividing unit is arguably the prey-predator pair; I count each species' own tracks as the claim does. The predators' approach to prey uses a written fuel-depletion drift, and their condensed state is written to depend on digestion (condensation only up q); their matter is never made from prey, so I do not mark E by construction. Overall merge/split 1.1 across both species (157 merges, 143 splits) because prey and predator bodies touch; per species 0.40 and 0.20. No Laplacian-only twin.
